episodes.title: 2 Hours of Skyrim's Darkest Mysteries to Fall Asleep To
episodes.angle: A calm journey from local investigations to buried histories and Daedric bargains; some mysteries are solved by their quests, others remain genuinely open.
episodes.scope: The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim base game, Dawnguard and Dragonborn. Full spoilers. No mods or Creation Club material. Do not develop the Dwemer disappearance: that has its own film.
episodes.planned_runtime: At least 150 minutes at 170 words per minute; estimate only.
forbidden: Original English narration only; no copied dialogue or competitor wording.
No invented journals, props, motives, dates, numerical probabilities or developer intent.
No mods, fan fiction, cut quests presented as playable canon, or unofficial endings.
No graphic violence or described self-harm methods; discuss consequences gently.
Only one optional subscribe plus listening location/day-or-night CTA in chapter one.
No trailers, repeated bedtime instructions, philosophical filler, repeated disclaimers or recaps.
All assigned chapters belong to one continuous narration. Resolve their local questions.
No claim the entire catalogue is unsolved. No wholesale plot retelling of the Dwemer film.

proof.primary: Skyrim: Laid to Rest, Helgi and Alva dialogue, Alva's journal.
proof.facts: Hroggar survives the fire that kills his family and moves in with Alva. Helgi appears as a ghost. Laelette is a vampire. Alva's journal connects her to Movarth. The town can confront the threat in Movarth's Lair. The quest supplies an answer, although the townspeople begin with an incomplete explanation.
proof.boundary: Do not imply that every mystery in this video stays unsolved. Keep the child's fate non-graphic. No invented original cause of vampirism.

proof.primary: Skyrim: Frostflow Abyss, Habd's, Ramati's and Sudi's journals, Mani's letter.
proof.facts: Habd and Ramati live at Frostflow with Sudi and Mani. The family journals record disagreement over the move and noises beneath the home. A passage leads to Falmer and chaurus below. Habd's remains can be recovered and placed at the lighthouse beacon, granting Sailor's Repose.
proof.boundary: Do not describe self-harm instructions or invent the exact last conversation. No precise egg counts or dates.

proof.primary: Skyrim: In My Time of Need, Saadia and Kematu dialogue.
proof.facts: Saadia works at the Bannered Mare and identifies herself as Iman, a noblewoman from Hammerfell. She says the Alik'r pursue her for opposing the Dominion. Kematu says she betrayed Taneth and is wanted for judgment in Hammerfell. Kematu can paralyze her at the stables if the player cooperates. The player can instead kill him and protect her.
proof.boundary: Neither account is confirmed as the whole truth. An urn appearing through NPC cleanup mechanics is not proof of an offscreen execution. Do not import a mod's letter.

proof.primary: Skyrim: The Raid and Supply and Demand, Wujeeta dialogue, Sarthis's note.
proof.facts: Wujeeta's addiction can be treated with a healing potion. She identifies Sarthis Idren as her supplier. The jarl authorizes investigation of Riften Warehouse. Sarthis and Orini Dral are encountered there; a note points to Cragslane Cavern and its operation. Disrupting the operation can help the player become thane.
proof.boundary: Do not claim this proves Maven personally runs every skooma shipment. No real-world drug preparation detail.

proof.primary: Skyrim: Blood on the Ice, Hjerim journals, Wuunferth and Calixto dialogue.
proof.facts: Windhelm has a series of murders. Hjerim contains incriminating material and a strange amulet. Calixto presents himself as an expert. Wuunferth can be wrongly accused; speaking with him can instead lead to an intervention at night. Calixto is revealed as the killer.
proof.boundary: Do not confuse Calixto with Wuunferth or promise the bug-prone quest always unfolds identically. No detailed mutilation.

proof.primary: Skyrim: The Forsworn Conspiracy, Nepos, Thonar and Eltrys dialogue.
proof.facts: A marketplace attack begins The Forsworn Conspiracy. Eltrys asks the player to investigate. Nepos admits serving Madanach. Thonar Silver-Blood has used imprisoned Forsworn for his purposes. The investigation leads to the player's arrest and Cidhna Mine.
proof.boundary: The Forsworn are not a single innocent or uniformly loyal group. Do not invent a signed conspiracy linking every guard or resident.

proof.primary: Skyrim: No One Escapes Cidhna Mine, Braig, Borkul and Madanach dialogue.
proof.facts: Madanach leads followers while imprisoned. Borkul guards access to him. Braig recounts his family's suffering. Madanach proposes an escape through a hidden route. The player can cooperate or oppose him, producing different outcomes and rewards involving Thonar.
proof.boundary: No single branch is the canon ending. Do not equate a player helping one escape with solving the whole Reach conflict.

proof.primary: Skyrim: The Man Who Cried Wolf, The Wolf Queen Awakened, Falk and Styrr dialogue.
proof.facts: Falk Firebeard sends the player to Wolfskull Cave in The Man Who Cried Wolf. Necromancers attempt to summon and bind Potema. A later quest, The Wolf Queen Awakened, takes the player below Solitude. Styrr explains the danger and the remains must be consecrated.
proof.boundary: Do not claim Potema is restored to normal bodily rule. No manufactured historical dates or motives beyond the books and dialogue.

proof.primary: Skyrim: Innocence Lost, With Friends Like These, Destroy the Dark Brotherhood.
proof.facts: Aventus Aretino performs the Black Sacrament after fleeing Honorhall. Grelod mistreats the children. The player can fulfill Aventus's request. A later encounter with Astrid initiates With Friends Like These; the player can join or destroy the Dark Brotherhood.
proof.boundary: Avoid graphic ritual instructions. Do not state Sithis personally ordered Grelod's death or that the player must join the Brotherhood.

proof.primary: Skyrim: Whispers in the Dark through Death Incarnate, Astrid confession, Night Mother dialogue.

proof.primary: Skyrim: Winterhold dialogue, Korir and College members; On the Great Collapse.
proof.facts: Much of Winterhold fell into the Sea of Ghosts during the Great Collapse in 4E 122. The College survived while much of the city did not. Jarl Korir distrusts the College; the mages deny causing the collapse. The exact cause is unresolved in Skyrim.
proof.boundary: Do not connect the later discovery of the Eye to the older collapse as confirmed causation. No time-loop solution or stated Augur culpability.

proof.primary: Skyrim: Under Saarthal, Tolfdir dialogue, Good Intentions.
proof.facts: Students visit Saarthal with Tolfdir. A Psijic warning appears. A large magical orb lies behind Jyrik Gauldurson. The College moves it to the Hall of the Elements. Tolfdir cannot identify its markings. It is called the Eye of Magnus, but its full origin is not explained.
proof.boundary: Do not assert it contains Magnus or a time machine. Gauldur's wider family story belongs to a later chapter.

proof.primary: Skyrim: Good Intentions, Tolfdir, Augur dialogue; Restoration Ritual Spell.
proof.facts: The Augur is encountered as a luminous magical presence beneath the College. Tolfdir remembers his talent and ambition. The Augur directs the player toward the Staff of Magnus to address the danger posed by the Eye. He also appears in the Restoration Ritual Spell quest.
proof.boundary: No exact age, undocumented experiment mechanism or claim he is Magnus. Do not use his knowledge as proof he caused unrelated events.

proof.primary: Skyrim: The Staff of Magnus, The Eye of Magnus, Labyrinthian echoes.
proof.facts: Echoes show the earlier College expedition losing members in Labyrinthian. Savos left companions sustaining the containment of Morokei. proof.primary: Skyrim: Forbidden Legend, Lost Legends, Daynas Valen's notes, writs of sealing.
proof.facts: Lost Legends introduces Gauldur. Daynas Valen investigates the suppressed story. Mikrul, Jyrik and Sigdis hold fragments at Folgunthur, Saarthal and Geirmund's Hall. Their fragments can be reunited at Reachwater Rock, where Gauldur's presence ends the confrontation.
proof.boundary: Do not invent the precise legal order erasing Gauldur or assert every detail of the legend has independent witnesses.

proof.primary: Skyrim: Evil in Waiting, Valdar dialogue and Valthume.
proof.facts: Valdar's ghost guards Hevnoraak in Valthume. He asks the player to recover three vessels. The recovered vessels permit a confrontation in which the player can defeat the dragon priest. Valdar's task can finally end.
proof.boundary: No invented alchemical formula, blood ritual instructions or universal theory of all dragon-priest resurrection.

proof.primary: Skyrim: Siege on the Dragon Cult, Skorm Snow-Strider's journal, Valmir's orders.
proof.facts: Valmir sends the player into Forelhost and wears an allegiance-dependent uniform. The ruin contains Skorm Snow-Strider's journal and traces of the besieged dragon cult. Rahgot remains within. A note exposes Valmir's connection to the Thalmor.
proof.boundary: Keep the cult's grim end non-graphic. No claim every dragon cult fortress followed the same end or that Valmir's disguise is identical in every playthrough.

proof.primary: Skyrim: Bromjunaar Sanctuary, wooden mask, dragon-priest mask puzzle.
proof.facts: A wooden mask found at the ruined sanctuary near Labyrinthian transports the wearer to an intact version. Eight named masks can be placed on busts, revealing Konahrik. Removing the wooden mask returns the player. Konahrik's original bearer is not identified by this puzzle.
proof.boundary: No confirmed time-travel mechanics beyond the shown displacement. No assertion that Konahrik was Vahlok, Shalidor or the player.

proof.primary: Skyrim: The Pale Lady; Eisa's Journal, Kyr's Log, Ra'jirr's Note; Frostmere Depths encounter.
proof.facts: Eisa is attacked outside Frostmere Crypt. Kyr has claimed a blade found by the gang. Ra'jirr is troubled by the Pale Lady in dreams and steals it to return it. Eisa's journal, Kyr's log and Ra'jirr's note explain the conflict. Kyr is dying inside; Ra'jirr confronts the spirit. The blade can be placed back at its monument to banish the Pale Lady, or the spirit can be defeated and the Pale Blade retained.
proof.boundary: Do not invent the spirit's original identity or a settled account of its binding. Treat keeping and returning the sword as alternate player choices.

proof.primary: Skyrim: The Throat of the World, Paarthurnax quest, Delphine and Arngeir dialogue.
proof.facts: Paarthurnax once served Alduin and later helped mortals learn the Voice. He teaches the Dragonborn at the Throat of the World. The Blades demand his death for his past. The Greybeards oppose killing him. The player may refuse or comply.
proof.boundary: Do not promise he can never become dangerous or assert he secretly plans to conquer Skyrim. No real-world morality lecture.

proof.primary: Skyrim: Alduin's Bane, Dragonslayer, Paarthurnax post-quest dialogue.
proof.facts: An Elder Scroll lets the Dragonborn witness the ancient confrontation at the Time-Wound. The Tongues use Dragonrend and the Scroll to cast Alduin forward in time. The Dragonborn later defeats him in Sovngarde. Alduin's soul is not absorbed in the usual dragon fashion; his ultimate cosmic role is left open.
proof.boundary: Do not claim Alduin is simply Akatosh, that his soul enters the player or that a future return is confirmed.

proof.primary: Skyrim: Waking Nightmare, Erandur dialogue, Vaermina's Torpor sequence.
proof.facts: Dawnstar suffers shared nightmares. Erandur leads the player into Nightcaller Temple and reveals his former identity as Casimir. Vaermina's Torpor permits a dream journey into a past incident. At the Skull, Vaermina urges the player to kill Erandur; he can instead complete the destruction ritual.
proof.boundary: Do not present Vaermina's accusation as verified. Avoid describing potion-making instructions or inventing a canon choice.

proof.primary: Skyrim: The Black Star, Nelacar, Aranea and Malyn dialogue.
proof.facts: Aranea sends the player to find Azura's Star. Nelacar explains Malyn Varen's work at Ilinalta's Deep. Malyn persists within the damaged artifact. The player enters it to defeat him. Aranea's path restores Azura's Star, while Nelacar's path produces the Black Star.
proof.boundary: Do not claim either artifact automatically frees all souls or that one outcome is the canon ending.

proof.primary: Skyrim: The Only Cure, Kesh and Peryite dialogue, Bthardamz.
proof.facts: Kesh leads the player to an audience with Peryite. Peryite sends the player after Orchendor, who has abandoned his intended role. Orchendor and the afflicted occupy Bthardamz. The player can receive Spellbreaker after defeating him.
proof.boundary: Do not assert the afflicted are simply cured at the end or generalize the disease into an unsupported world-ending plague. No detailed incense recipe.

proof.primary: Skyrim Dawnguard: Touching the Sky, Gelebor, Vyrthur and Serana dialogue.
proof.facts: Gelebor is a surviving Snow Elf knight-paladin in the Forgotten Vale. A pilgrimage through wayshrines leads to Auriel's Bow. Vyrthur is a vampire and reveals his role in creating the prophecy pursued by Harkon. Serana confronts him. Gelebor speaks about the Falmer with grief and caution.
proof.boundary: Do not retell the whole Dwemer/Falmer history here; it belongs to the dedicated film. Do not invent how many uncorrupted Snow Elves survive elsewhere.

proof.primary: Skyrim Dragonborn: Dragonborn, The Temple of Miraak, The Fate of the Skaal, At the Summit of Apocrypha.
proof.facts: Miraak's cultists target the Dragonborn. People on Solstheim work at All-Maker Stones under compulsion. Frea resists and accompanies the player. Black Books lead to Apocrypha. Miraak seeks escape from Hermaeus Mora and can steal dragon souls the player has earned.
proof.boundary: No exact number of years in Apocrypha or assertion the player must become Mora's permanent willing servant.

proof.primary: Skyrim Dragonborn: Unearthed, The Journal of Ralis Sedarys, volumes 19-23.
proof.facts: Ralis Sedarys asks for money to excavate Kolbjorn Barrow. Successive visits open deeper chambers, uncover artifacts and find dead workers. His journals change as Ahzidal's influence grows. The final confrontation reveals Ralis summoning the dragon priest. The player may spare or kill Ralis. Later excavation journals implicate Ralis in sacrificing workers for Ahzidal's return; his claimed loss of control remains distinct from that implication.
proof.boundary: No unquestionable psychiatric or possession diagnosis beyond the quest's evidence. No invented survivor testimony. Avoid unnecessary exact body counts.

proof.primary: Skyrim Dragonborn: The Path of Knowledge, The Gardener of Men, At the Summit of Apocrypha.
proof.facts: Neloth studies the Black Books and helps locate one at Nchardak. Hermaeus Mora demands the Skaal's secrets; Storn agrees and dies during the transfer. The Dragonborn learns the final Bend Will word and confronts Miraak. Mora kills Miraak after his defeat. Frea warns the player to remain alert to Mora's influence.
proof.boundary: Do not declare the player finally free of every Daedric claim or forever enslaved. No recap, CTA, next-video promise or new unrelated mystery.

The blade can be placed back at its monument to banish the Pale Lady, or the spirit can be defeated and the Pale Blade retained.

chapters.job: Develop Paarthurnax, the Greybeards and the Blades through the actual dilemma after the main story reveals his identity. Explain his past, teaching, the nature of dragon dominance and the different choices without electing a canon ending.
chapters.facts: Paarthurnax once served Alduin and later helped mortals learn the Voice. He teaches the Dragonborn at the Throat of the World. The Blades demand his death for his past. The Greybeards oppose killing him. The player may refuse or comply.

episodes.title: The Secrets of Vault-Tec Explained to Fall Asleep To | Fallout Lore
episodes.angle: Follow the practical promise of shelter, the experiments hidden from residents, resistance by individuals and the communities that survive beyond the vaults.
episodes.scope: Games only: Fallout, Fallout 2, Fallout 3, Fallout New Vegas and its Honest Hearts expansion, Fallout 4 with Far Harbor and Vault-Tec Workshop, plus the original Vault 76 overseer and Reclamation story. Full spoilers. Exclude the TV series, Fallout Bible-only claims and later live-service additions.
episodes.planned_runtime: At least 150 minutes at 170 words per minute; estimate only.
forbidden: Original English narration only; no copied dialogue or competitor wording.
No invented journals, props, motives, dates, numerical probabilities or developer intent.
No mods, fan fiction, cut quests presented as playable canon, or unofficial endings.
No graphic violence or described self-harm methods; discuss consequences gently.
Only one optional subscribe plus listening location/day-or-night CTA in chapter one.
No trailers, repeated bedtime instructions, philosophical filler, repeated disclaimers or recaps.
All assigned chapters belong to one continuous narration. Resolve their local questions.

Do not state Vault-Tec definitively started the nuclear war. No TV vaults 31/32/33 or characters. No universal space-colony explanation. No claim every vault was an experiment, every experiment failed identically, or Vault-Tec was omniscient.

proof.primary: Fallout 4: Out of Time, Vault 111 terminal entries and opening sequence.
proof.facts: In Fallout 4 the player's family enters Vault 111 as bombs fall. Residents are placed in cryogenic pods under the pretense of decontamination. The Sole Survivor later witnesses Shaun's abduction and eventually wakes to an abandoned vault. Staff knew about a long-term cryogenic observation experiment that residents did not.
proof.boundary: Do not claim Vault-Tec itself ordered Kellogg's kidnapping; that is an Institute operation. No exact runtime promise.

proof.primary: Fallout 4: Vault 111 security, overseer and monitoring terminals.
proof.facts: Vault 111 staff monitor frozen residents. Security and scientists receive different responsibilities and access. The all-clear signal fails to arrive; food shortages create conflict with the overseer and a mutiny. Later pod failures and Institute interference belong to another phase of the vault's history.
proof.boundary: Do not make every pod death an immediate result of the staff mutiny or pretend the overseer planned the Institute's actions.

proof.primary: Fallout 4 opening, Vault-Tec representative; Fallout 1 Vault Dweller's Survival Guide; in-game vault interiors.
proof.facts: Vault-Tec markets underground shelters before the Great War. Vaults contain living quarters, life-support machinery, medical facilities and governance under overseers. Fallout 4 shows a representative registering the family. Vault-Tec branding remains in manuals, posters, terminals and training material after the war.
proof.boundary: Do not say every Vault-Tec employee knew every experiment, or that no vault saved anyone. No unsupported total count or per-vault price.

proof.primary: Fallout: Vault 13 overseer dialogue, water-chip quest, Necropolis.
proof.facts: Fallout begins with Vault 13's water purification chip failing. The Vault Dweller is sent outside to find a replacement. Vault 15 cannot solve the problem; the journey eventually leads to a replacement in Necropolis. The outside contains settlements and trading networks despite the vault's isolation.
proof.boundary: No claim the chip was deliberately sabotaged; Fallout does not establish that. Do not prescribe one player route as mandatory.

proof.primary: Fallout ending, Fallout 2 opening and President Richardson dialogue.
proof.facts: The Vault Dweller can defeat the Master and the super mutant threat. The overseer then exiles the protagonist, fearing others will follow the example and leave. The Vault Dweller's descendants establish Arroyo. In Fallout 2, President Richardson describes the vault program as an experiment and Vault 13 as a source of untainted test subjects.
proof.boundary: Do not call the Fallout Bible's 200-year isolation plan definitive game canon. Do not assert the overseer knows Richardson's later plan.

proof.primary: Fallout 2: Arroyo, Vault City and Vault 13; Fallout 3: Finding the Garden of Eden.
proof.facts: The Garden of Eden Creation Kit is a vault-associated rebuilding resource. The Chosen One seeks one for Arroyo in Fallout 2. Vault City used a G.E.C.K. to develop its settlement. A G.E.C.K. is sought for Project Purity in Fallout 3 and retrieved from Vault 87.
proof.boundary: Different games depict or describe its capabilities differently. Do not invent one universal engineering mechanism, limitless transformation radius or instant city construction.

proof.primary: Fallout 2: Vault City, Vault 8, First Citizen Lynette and citizenship dialogue.
proof.facts: Vault 8 becomes the foundation of Vault City. Its people use a G.E.C.K. and retain advanced technology, medical capability and a power structure distinguishing citizens from outsiders and servants. The old vault remains part of the settlement rather than an unexplored death trap.
proof.boundary: Do not equate control vault with moral utopia or repeat an unverified official opening date. No claim every resident supports every policy.

proof.primary: Fallout: Vault 15 and Shady Sands; Fallout 2: Vault 15, Darion and the squatters.
proof.facts: Vault 15 is an unsuccessful early destination in Fallout. Its former inhabitants contribute to Shady Sands and groups including the Khans. Fallout 2 returns to the site, where Darion's New Khans and displaced squatters complicate the NCR's interest in the vault and its computer.
proof.boundary: Do not treat every later conflict as proof each resident was personally selected to become a raider. Avoid the non-game experimental demographics as established dialogue.

proof.primary: Fallout: Necropolis, Set, underground ghouls, Vault 12 water system.
proof.facts: Necropolis contains ghouls, Vault 12 and the working chip needed by Vault 13. Removing the chip threatens their water supply unless another solution is arranged. Set and the underground ghoul community have different relationships with the visitor. Vault 12's failed sealing exposes its residents to radiation.
proof.boundary: Do not turn every detail of Fallout Bible design notes into a spoken proven experiment order. Ghoulification is not a guaranteed universal outcome of radiation.

proof.primary: Fallout 3: Growing Up Fast, Future Imperfect, Escape!, James dialogue and Vault 101 records.
proof.facts: Fallout 3's protagonist grows up in Vault 101 under an overseer. James leaves and the vault erupts in crisis. The player later learns James and the infant protagonist were admitted from outside. Vault 101's story of absolute isolation is therefore incomplete.
proof.boundary: Do not claim the protagonist was born inside Vault 101 or that every resident knew James's earlier life.

proof.primary: Fallout 3: Trouble on the Homefront, Amata, overseer and resident dialogue.
proof.facts: A distress signal can bring the Lone Wanderer back to Vault 101. Amata and others want change. The player can negotiate, enforce isolation or cause destructive outcomes depending on choices. Even a peaceful opening does not necessarily mean the protagonist can simply resume childhood there.
proof.boundary: No single canon political result. Do not describe the quest as inevitably available after any ending or every prior choice.

proof.primary: Fallout 3: Tranquility Lane, Braun and Dithers dialogue, abandoned house terminal.
proof.facts: Stanislaus Braun maintains residents inside a virtual reality system at Vault 112. In Tranquility Lane he appears as Betty. James is trapped in the simulation. Old Lady Dithers recognizes that the neighborhood is artificial and points toward the failsafe. The player can activate it instead of following Braun's cruel tasks.
proof.boundary: No step-by-step graphic violence; no assertion a simulation is harmless or that Braun can be simply killed in the same manner as its residents.

proof.primary: Fallout 3: Agatha's Song, Vault 92 terminals and Zoe Hammerstein recordings.
proof.facts: Vault 92 recruits skilled musicians. A white-noise project introduces subliminal conditioning and produces dangerous psychological effects. Researcher records and Zoe Hammerstein's recordings reveal the decline. Agatha asks the player to recover the Soil Stradivarius violin from the vault. Agatha's inherited family letters concern Hilda, the ancestor connected with the Soil Stradivarius and Vault 92. Zoe Hammerstein is a separate recorded resident, not Agatha's ancestor. Agatha's dialogue describes Hilda's violin and entry into the vault.
proof.boundary: Do not invent real scientific efficacy for subliminal control. No exact percentages or body counts. Music is not itself the cause of the catastrophe.

proof.primary: Fallout 3: Vault 106 terminals and exploration sequences.
proof.facts: Vault 106's population is exposed to psychoactive chemicals through its ventilation system. The exploring Lone Wanderer experiences hallucinations, including figures associated with Vault 101. Hostile survivors remain in the vault. The environmental danger continues after the original experiment begins.
proof.boundary: No invented chemical formula, precise modern pharmacology or confident biography for each attacker. Hallucinated James is not actual evidence he visited the vault.

proof.primary: Fallout 3: Vault 108 cloning log and overseer planning records.
proof.facts: Vault 108 contains hostile clones named Gary. Research records document cloning and mounting difficulty handling the copies. Vault planning also creates unstable leadership and resource conditions. The result encountered by the player is a damaged vault populated by copies rather than a functioning community.
proof.boundary: Do not assert every clone has identical memories, that Gary is an immortal single mind or that a fully known final revolt explains every corpse.

proof.primary: Fallout 3: Finding the Garden of Eden, Vault 87 terminals, Fawkes dialogue.
proof.facts: Vault 87 houses FEV experiments and becomes a source of Capital Wasteland super mutants. Fawkes is imprisoned but retains unusual intelligence and can help retrieve the G.E.C.K. The player's route through Little Lamplight leads into the facility; the surface entrance is heavily irradiated.
proof.boundary: Not every super mutant in the franchise originates at Vault 87. Do not equate all FEV strains, ghoulification and radiation mutations.

proof.primary: Fallout New Vegas: Vault 11 posters, election records and Gus Olson's speech.
proof.facts: Vault 11's residents are told they must provide one sacrifice each year or the population will die. They choose the overseer as that sacrifice after punishing the initial overseer. Voting blocs emerge; candidates campaign to avoid being elected. The Justice Bloc gains substantial influence.
proof.boundary: Do not reveal the final refusal twice or claim the residents originally consented to sacrifice before entering. Avoid quoting the election posters.

proof.primary: Fallout New Vegas: Vault 11 Katherine deposition, overseer order, automated response and final recording.
proof.facts: Katherine Stone opposes the Justice Bloc after its coercion and betrayal. As overseer she changes the sacrifice selection system. Conflict devastates the vault. The final survivors refuse another sacrifice and the computer reveals the supposed collective death threat was a test. A recording and remains at the entrance show the survivors' despair; one walks away.
proof.boundary: Do not assert the survivor is a named New Vegas character. No detailed sexual violence or self-harm method. The computer's congratulation does not undo what happened.

proof.primary: Fallout New Vegas: There Stands the Grass, Vault 22 records, Hildern and Keely dialogue.
proof.facts: Dr. Hildern at the NCR's Camp McCarran seeks agricultural research from Vault 22. Keely has entered before the Courier. Plant research is associated with a dangerous spore infection and spore carriers. Keely wants the data destroyed; the Courier has different options.
proof.boundary: Do not claim every plant in the Mojave is infected. No real-world pathogen cultivation or ignition instructions. The data's usefulness does not mean its methods were safe.

proof.primary: Fallout New Vegas Honest Hearts: Randall Clark's terminal records, Vault 22 dwellers' note, Sorrows dialogue.
proof.facts: Randall Clark's terminals in Zion record encounters with refugees from Vault 22. They carry the spore-associated danger and attack others in the canyon. Clark opposes them. His later help to a different group of children becomes part of the Sorrows' inherited Father in the Caves tradition.
proof.boundary: Do not conflate the Vault 22 refugees with the children Clark later helps or make the Sorrows direct biological descendants of those infected aggressors.

proof.primary: Fallout New Vegas: Hard Luck Blues, Vault 34 terminals, sharecropper dialogue.
proof.facts: Vault 34 has an extensive armory and suffers internal conflict and reactor trouble. Radiation affects the NCR sharecropper farms. A distress message indicates survivors remain trapped. At the control terminal the Courier chooses whether to divert power to help them or shut down the reactor to address the contamination.
proof.boundary: No assertion a clever third option safely saves everyone. Do not declare one branch canon or invent survivors seen when the chosen branch does not show them.

proof.primary: Fallout New Vegas: Nellis, Pearl, Pete, Loyal, Volare!
proof.facts: The Boomers descend from people who left Vault 34 with weapons and established themselves at Nellis Air Force Base. Pearl leads them. Pete presents their history. They are protective of their isolation and can enlist the Courier in raising a bomber from Lake Mead.
proof.boundary: Do not claim every Vault 34 resident left with them or that their history resolves the later reactor disaster. No real weapons operating guide.

proof.primary: Fallout New Vegas: Vault 21, Sarah Weintraub and Michael Angelo dialogue.
proof.facts: Vault 21 resolves disputes through gambling. Mr. House wins control through a wager accepted by its residents. Much of the vault is filled with concrete, while an accessible section becomes a hotel managed by Sarah Weintraub. Some former residents establish lives elsewhere on the Strip.
proof.boundary: Do not invent a secret army in the sealed sections or claim the wager had informed consent from every person. No exact concrete quantity.

proof.primary: Fallout 4: Vault 81 original overseer's terminal, research communication terminal.
proof.facts: Overseer Dr. Olivette opposes the planned use of residents as disease subjects. Only a small research team reaches the hidden section; she prevents the intended experiment on the population. The public vault develops into a functioning community while the separated researchers continue work with limited resources.
proof.boundary: Her correct name is Olivette, not Olivia, and she is distinct from current overseer Gwen McNamara. Vault 81 was not designed as a control vault.

proof.primary: Fallout 4: Hole in the Wall, Curie dialogue, research laboratory records.
proof.facts: Austin falls ill after a mole-rat bite. The Sole Survivor explores the hidden lab and finds Curie, who has developed a cure. A single available dose creates a choice if the protagonist was infected. Curie can leave the vault and later pursue a new form and research with the player.
proof.boundary: Do not imply the treatment immediately cures every disease or that Curie herself initiated Olivette's sabotage. No claim the protagonist always becomes infected.

proof.primary: Fallout 4: Vault 95 resident records and Vault-Tec agent log, Benign Intervention.
proof.facts: Vault 95 gathers people recovering from addiction and supports a period of sobriety. A concealed Vault-Tec agent opens a hidden supply of addictive substances after five years, provoking the planned crisis. Long afterward, Cait can seek treatment with the Sole Survivor at its surviving detox facility.
proof.boundary: Do not say the treatment guarantees an uncomplicated lifelong recovery. No drug recipes, modern medical advice or invented relapse rates.

proof.primary: Fallout 4: Unlikely Valentine, Vault 114 interviews; Far Harbor: Brain Dead, Vault 118 terminals.
proof.facts: Vault 114 is reached through Park Street Station; Nick Valentine is held there by Skinny Malone's gang. Its intended experiment places wealthy residents under poor conditions and an unsuitable overseer chosen through interviews including Soup Can Harry. Vault 118 beneath the Cliff's Edge Hotel was intended to divide rich and poor, but only the wealthy section was completed and its residents became robobrains. Brain Dead investigates a later murder there. Brain Dead reveals that Ezra killed Julianna Riggs after she discovered his embezzlement, then impersonated her and made the victim appear to be Ezra. The detective can expose him and choose how to respond.
proof.boundary: Do not describe either original social experiment as completed exactly as planned. Do not conflate Nick with a Vault-Tec creation, or reveal an invented Vault 118 ending.

proof.primary: Fallout 4 Vault-Tec Workshop: Vault 88, Barstow, Clem and experiment configuration choices.
proof.facts: Overseer Barstow survives as a ghoul in unfinished Vault 88. The Sole Survivor can build a settlement and assist her experiments with Clem and other volunteers. The experiments have different selectable parameters, including less harmful options. The player can oppose Barstow or continue along her preferred direction.
proof.boundary: No one ending is compulsory. Do not list the most harmful device settings as a how-to or claim a voluntary building task gives residents full knowledge of every hidden parameter.

proof.primary: Fallout 76: Vault 76 terminal entries, overseer's mission and original journey holotapes.
proof.facts: Vault 76 is a control vault with a population chosen to rebuild. Its residents leave on Reclamation Day. The overseer is separately ordered to secure nuclear silos Alpha, Bravo and Charlie for Vault-Tec, disregarding competing claims. Her recordings follow her discovery of devastated Appalachia and growing doubts about the organization's judgment.
proof.boundary: Use the original Fallout 76 vault and overseer story, not current live-service developments. Do not assert Vault-Tec launched the first bombs, a confirmed space-colony master plan, or that every vault was intended to kill everyone. No recap catalogue or CTA.

chapters.boundary: Do not claim Vault-Tec itself ordered Kellogg's kidnapping; that is an Institute operation. No exact runtime promise.
chapters.primary_evidence: Fallout 4: Out of Time, Vault 111 terminal entries and opening sequence.

chapters.title: The staff on the other side
chapters.job: Stay in Vault 111 but switch to the observing staff, their restricted supplies, expected all-clear and conflict. Explain why the staff's collapse is distinct from the much later Institute interference.

The all-clear signal fails to arrive; food shortages create conflict with the overseer and a mutiny. Later pod failures and Institute interference belong to another phase of the vault's history.
chapters.boundary: Do not make every pod death an immediate result of the staff mutiny or pretend the overseer planned the Institute's actions.

chapters.title: The public promise
chapters.job: Explain the publicly sold promise through the Vault-Tec representative, vault advertisements, assigned jumpsuits, Pip-Boy and overseer office. Give practical shelter systems and why people reasonably sought them. Contrast marketing with actual unequal information, using only already named examples briefly.
chapters.facts: Vault-Tec markets underground shelters before the Great War. Vaults contain living quarters, life-support machinery, medical facilities and governance under overseers. Fallout 4 shows a representative registering the family. Vault-Tec branding remains in manuals, posters, terminals and training material after the war.
chapters.boundary: Do not say every Vault-Tec employee knew every experiment, or that no vault saved anyone. No unsupported total count or per-vault price.
chapters.primary_evidence: Fallout 4 opening, Vault-Tec representative; Fallout 1 Vault Dweller's Survival Guide; in-game vault interiors.
chapters.length: 950-1100 substantive words; use the factual developments assigned here, never padding.

chapters.title: A water chip and an open door
chapters.job: Follow Vault 13 in the original Fallout: the failed chip, the chosen errand, Junktown and the Hub as evidence of a living outside world, and the return. Explain why one technical failure changes a resident's relationship to the shelter.
chapters.facts: Fallout begins with Vault 13's water purification chip failing. The Vault Dweller is sent outside to find a replacement. Vault 15 cannot solve the problem; the journey eventually leads to a replacement in Necropolis. The outside contains settlements and trading networks despite the vault's isolation.
chapters.boundary: No claim the chip was deliberately sabotaged; Fallout does not establish that. Do not prescribe one player route as mandatory.
chapters.primary_evidence: Fallout: Vault 13 overseer dialogue, water-chip quest, Necropolis.
chapters.length: 950-1100 substantive words; use the factual developments assigned here, never padding.

chapters.title: The price of coming home
chapters.job: Continue Vault 13 through the defeat of the Master, the overseer's refusal to readmit the hero and the founding of Arroyo. Explain the later Enclave revelation through Richardson's words, carefully separating a villain's account from Fallout Bible cut background.
chapters.facts: The Vault Dweller can defeat the Master and the super mutant threat. The overseer then exiles the protagonist, fearing others will follow the example and leave. The Vault Dweller's descendants establish Arroyo. In Fallout 2, President Richardson describes the vault program as an experiment and Vault 13 as a source of untainted test subjects.
chapters.boundary: Do not call the Fallout Bible's 200-year isolation plan definitive game canon. Do not assert the overseer knows Richardson's later plan.
chapters.primary_evidence: Fallout ending, Fallout 2 opening and President Richardson dialogue.
chapters.length: 950-1100 substantive words; use the factual developments assigned here, never padding.

chapters.title: The garden in a suitcase
chapters.job: Explain the G.E.C.K. across its actual uses: Arroyo's search, Vault City's flourishing ground and Fallout 3's purifier. Develop the promise of rebuilding with people who need water and workable land, rather than an all-powerful magic box.
chapters.facts: The Garden of Eden Creation Kit is a vault-associated rebuilding resource. The Chosen One seeks one for Arroyo in Fallout 2. Vault City used a G.E.C.K. to develop its settlement. A G.E.C.K. is sought for Project Purity in Fallout 3 and retrieved from Vault 87.
chapters.boundary: Different games depict or describe its capabilities differently. Do not invent one universal engineering mechanism, limitless transformation radius or instant city construction.
chapters.primary_evidence: Fallout 2: Arroyo, Vault City and Vault 13; Fallout 3: Finding the Garden of Eden.
chapters.length: 950-1100 substantive words; use the factual developments assigned here, never padding.

chapters.title: The vault that became a city
chapters.job: Explore Vault City as the productive inheritance of a working shelter and a harsh social order. Show the transition to surface settlement, citizenship, outsider treatment and dependency on systems and labor.
chapters.facts: Vault 8 becomes the foundation of Vault City. Its people use a G.E.C.K. and retain advanced technology, medical capability and a power structure distinguishing citizens from outsiders and servants. The old vault remains part of the settlement rather than an unexplored death trap.
chapters.boundary: Do not equate control vault with moral utopia or repeat an unverified official opening date. No claim every resident supports every policy.
chapters.primary_evidence: Fallout 2: Vault City, Vault 8, First Citizen Lynette and citizenship dialogue.
chapters.length: 950-1100 substantive words; use the factual developments assigned here, never padding.

chapters.title: The people who left Vault 15
chapters.job: Develop Vault 15 through the ruined destination in Fallout and the communities connected to its former population. Explain Shady Sands and the later confrontation with the squatters and Darion's Khans in Fallout 2.
chapters.facts: Vault 15 is an unsuccessful early destination in Fallout. Its former inhabitants contribute to Shady Sands and groups including the Khans. Fallout 2 returns to the site, where Darion's New Khans and displaced squatters complicate the NCR's interest in the vault and its computer.
chapters.boundary: Do not treat every later conflict as proof each resident was personally selected to become a raider. Avoid the non-game experimental demographics as established dialogue.
chapters.primary_evidence: Fallout: Vault 15 and Shady Sands; Fallout 2: Vault 15, Darion and the squatters.
chapters.length: 950-1100 substantive words; use the factual developments assigned here, never padding.

chapters.title: The door at Necropolis
chapters.job: Explain Vault 12 and the ghoul community at Necropolis through the water system, Set and the underground ghouls. Discuss the defective protective barrier and the player's choice about taking the chip while respecting version-specific background.
chapters.facts: Necropolis contains ghouls, Vault 12 and the working chip needed by Vault 13. Removing the chip threatens their water supply unless another solution is arranged. Set and the underground ghoul community have different relationships with the visitor. Vault 12's failed sealing exposes its residents to radiation.
chapters.boundary: Do not turn every detail of Fallout Bible design notes into a spoken proven experiment order. Ghoulification is not a guaranteed universal outcome of radiation.
chapters.primary_evidence: Fallout: Necropolis, Set, underground ghouls, Vault 12 water system.
chapters.length: 950-1100 substantive words; use the factual developments assigned here, never padding.

chapters.title: The vault that never opens
chapters.job: Follow Vault 101 through the Lone Wanderer's childhood, the G.O.A.T., James's departure and the security response. Explain how an account of permanent isolation is maintained as a household truth despite contact with the surface.
chapters.facts: Fallout 3's protagonist grows up in Vault 101 under an overseer. James leaves and the vault erupts in crisis. The player later learns James and the infant protagonist were admitted from outside. Vault 101's story of absolute isolation is therefore incomplete.
chapters.boundary: Do not claim the protagonist was born inside Vault 101 or that every resident knew James's earlier life.
chapters.primary_evidence: Fallout 3: Growing Up Fast, Future Imperfect, Escape!, James dialogue and Vault 101 records.
chapters.length: 950-1100 substantive words; use the factual developments assigned here, never padding.

chapters.title: Trouble at home
chapters.job: Return only for Trouble on the Homefront. Develop Amata's request, the arguments over opening, the overseer alternatives and the changed relationship between parent generation and children. Present branches fairly and leave their outcome conditional.
chapters.facts: A distress signal can bring the Lone Wanderer back to Vault 101. Amata and others want change. The player can negotiate, enforce isolation or cause destructive outcomes depending on choices. Even a peaceful opening does not necessarily mean the protagonist can simply resume childhood there.
chapters.boundary: No single canon political result. Do not describe the quest as inevitably available after any ending or every prior choice.
chapters.primary_evidence: Fallout 3: Trouble on the Homefront, Amata, overseer and resident dialogue.
chapters.length: 950-1100 substantive words; use the factual developments assigned here, never padding.

chapters.title: The town inside a machine
chapters.job: Explore Vault 112 as the contrast between preserved bodies and simulated lives. Follow James into Tranquility Lane, Betty, Old Lady Dithers and the failsafe. Explain the available release without dwelling on the tasks of cruelty.
chapters.facts: Stanislaus Braun maintains residents inside a virtual reality system at Vault 112. In Tranquility Lane he appears as Betty. James is trapped in the simulation. Old Lady Dithers recognizes that the neighborhood is artificial and points toward the failsafe. The player can activate it instead of following Braun's cruel tasks.
chapters.boundary: No step-by-step graphic violence; no assertion a simulation is harmless or that Braun can be simply killed in the same manner as its residents.
chapters.primary_evidence: Fallout 3: Tranquility Lane, Braun and Dithers dialogue, abandoned house terminal.
chapters.length: 950-1100 substantive words; use the factual developments assigned here, never padding.

chapters.title: The musicians of Vault 92
chapters.job: Develop the recruitment of musicians, white-noise experiment, disagreement among staff and Agatha's search for a violin. Show the difference between a preserved instrument and the failed community it outlives.
chapters.facts: Vault 92 recruits skilled musicians. A white-noise project introduces subliminal conditioning and produces dangerous psychological effects. Researcher records and Zoe Hammerstein's recordings reveal the decline. Agatha asks the player to recover the Soil Stradivarius violin from the vault. Agatha's inherited family letters concern Hilda, the ancestor connected with the Soil Stradivarius and Vault 92. Zoe Hammerstein is a separate recorded resident, not Agatha's ancestor. Agatha's dialogue describes Hilda's violin and entry into the vault.
chapters.boundary: Do not invent real scientific efficacy for subliminal control. No exact percentages or body counts. Music is not itself the cause of the catastrophe.
chapters.primary_evidence: Fallout 3: Agatha's Song, Vault 92 terminals and Zoe Hammerstein recordings.
chapters.length: 950-1100 substantive words; use the factual developments assigned here, never padding.

chapters.title: The air of Vault 106
chapters.job: Trace the player's altered perceptions through Vault 106 and compare visible attackers with hallucinated familiar figures. Explain the air experiment and the limitation it places on reading this particular ruin.
chapters.facts: Vault 106's population is exposed to psychoactive chemicals through its ventilation system. The exploring Lone Wanderer experiences hallucinations, including figures associated with Vault 101. Hostile survivors remain in the vault. The environmental danger continues after the original experiment begins.
chapters.boundary: No invented chemical formula, precise modern pharmacology or confident biography for each attacker. Hallucinated James is not actual evidence he visited the vault.
chapters.primary_evidence: Fallout 3: Vault 106 terminals and exploration sequences.
chapters.length: 950-1100 substantive words; use the factual developments assigned here, never padding.

chapters.title: The name repeated in Vault 108
chapters.job: Develop the clones and laboratory at Vault 108, then the leadership experiment and planned weaknesses in the vault. Explain what the presence of Gary copies shows without inventing a complete chronological rebellion.
chapters.facts: Vault 108 contains hostile clones named Gary. Research records document cloning and mounting difficulty handling the copies. Vault planning also creates unstable leadership and resource conditions. The result encountered by the player is a damaged vault populated by copies rather than a functioning community.
chapters.boundary: Do not assert every clone has identical memories, that Gary is an immortal single mind or that a fully known final revolt explains every corpse.
chapters.primary_evidence: Fallout 3: Vault 108 cloning log and overseer planning records.
chapters.length: 950-1100 substantive words; use the factual developments assigned here, never padding.

chapters.title: What Fawkes remembers
chapters.job: Explain Vault 87 through its FEV work, surviving research remains, Fawkes's confinement and the G.E.C.K. retrieval. Keep its local mutant origin distinct from other games' FEV programs.
chapters.facts: Vault 87 houses FEV experiments and becomes a source of Capital Wasteland super mutants. Fawkes is imprisoned but retains unusual intelligence and can help retrieve the G.E.C.K. The player's route through Little Lamplight leads into the facility; the surface entrance is heavily irradiated.
chapters.boundary: Not every super mutant in the franchise originates at Vault 87. Do not equate all FEV strains, ghoulification and radiation mutations.
chapters.primary_evidence: Fallout 3: Finding the Garden of Eden, Vault 87 terminals, Fawkes dialogue.
chapters.length: 950-1100 substantive words; use the factual developments assigned here, never padding.

chapters.title: The election nobody wanted
chapters.job: Introduce Vault 11 through campaign posters and the annual sacrifice demand. Follow the inversion of normal overseer ambition, voting blocs and the way residents normalize the imposed rule. Reserve Katherine's final intervention and the experiment's conclusion for the next chapter.
chapters.facts: Vault 11's residents are told they must provide one sacrifice each year or the population will die. They choose the overseer as that sacrifice after punishing the initial overseer. Voting blocs emerge; candidates campaign to avoid being elected. The Justice Bloc gains substantial influence.
chapters.boundary: Do not reveal the final refusal twice or claim the residents originally consented to sacrifice before entering. Avoid quoting the election posters.
chapters.primary_evidence: Fallout New Vegas: Vault 11 posters, election records and Gus Olson's speech.
chapters.length: 950-1100 substantive words; use the factual developments assigned here, never padding.

chapters.title: When Vault 11 finally refused
chapters.job: Continue with Katherine Stone's resistance, the change in selection, violent backlash and the final refusal. Treat coercion non-graphically. Explain the automated congratulatory response and the records near the exit with the uncertainty of the last person's identity.
chapters.facts: Katherine Stone opposes the Justice Bloc after its coercion and betrayal. As overseer she changes the sacrifice selection system. Conflict devastates the vault. The final survivors refuse another sacrifice and the computer reveals the supposed collective death threat was a test. A recording and remains at the entrance show the survivors' despair; one walks away.
chapters.boundary: Do not assert the survivor is a named New Vegas character. No detailed sexual violence or self-harm method. The computer's congratulation does not undo what happened.
chapters.primary_evidence: Fallout New Vegas: Vault 11 Katherine deposition, overseer order, automated response and final recording.
chapters.length: 950-1100 substantive words; use the factual developments assigned here, never padding.

chapters.title: The gardens of Vault 22
chapters.job: Follow the player's research assignment, Keely's investigation and the overgrown vault. Explain the spore problem, the attraction of agricultural data and the choice over its survival.
chapters.facts: Dr. Hildern at the NCR's Camp McCarran seeks agricultural research from Vault 22. Keely has entered before the Courier. Plant research is associated with a dangerous spore infection and spore carriers. Keely wants the data destroyed; the Courier has different options.
chapters.boundary: Do not claim every plant in the Mojave is infected. No real-world pathogen cultivation or ignition instructions. The data's usefulness does not mean its methods were safe.
chapters.primary_evidence: Fallout New Vegas: There Stands the Grass, Vault 22 records, Hildern and Keely dialogue.
chapters.length: 950-1100 substantive words; use the factual developments assigned here, never padding.

chapters.title: A memory carried to Zion
chapters.job: Use Honest Hearts to follow Vault 22 beyond its walls. Explain the historical refugees in Zion through Randall Clark's records, their disease and predation, and the distinction between those refugees and Zion's later tribes.
chapters.facts: Randall Clark's terminals in Zion record encounters with refugees from Vault 22. They carry the spore-associated danger and attack others in the canyon. Clark opposes them. His later help to a different group of children becomes part of the Sorrows' inherited Father in the Caves tradition.
chapters.boundary: Do not conflate the Vault 22 refugees with the children Clark later helps or make the Sorrows direct biological descendants of those infected aggressors.
chapters.primary_evidence: Fallout New Vegas Honest Hearts: Randall Clark's terminal records, Vault 22 dwellers' note, Sorrows dialogue.
chapters.length: 950-1100 substantive words; use the factual developments assigned here, never padding.

chapters.title: The reactor beneath the farms
chapters.job: Explore Vault 34 through its armory, reactor leak and trapped survivors. Follow Hard Luck Blues from the NCR sharecroppers to the terminal choice. Explain the immediate human cost of prioritizing either group.
chapters.facts: Vault 34 has an extensive armory and suffers internal conflict and reactor trouble. Radiation affects the NCR sharecropper farms. A distress message indicates survivors remain trapped. At the control terminal the Courier chooses whether to divert power to help them or shut down the reactor to address the contamination.
chapters.boundary: No assertion a clever third option safely saves everyone. Do not declare one branch canon or invent survivors seen when the chosen branch does not show them.
chapters.primary_evidence: Fallout New Vegas: Hard Luck Blues, Vault 34 terminals, sharecropper dialogue.
chapters.length: 950-1100 substantive words; use the factual developments assigned here, never padding.

chapters.title: The people who became the Boomers
chapters.job: Develop the Vault 34 emigrants who settle at Nellis separately from the reactor choice. Show how Pearl's community remembers its origin, why outsiders fear the artillery and how the Lady in the Water quest changes their isolation.
chapters.facts: The Boomers descend from people who left Vault 34 with weapons and established themselves at Nellis Air Force Base. Pearl leads them. Pete presents their history. They are protective of their isolation and can enlist the Courier in raising a bomber from Lake Mead.
chapters.boundary: Do not claim every Vault 34 resident left with them or that their history resolves the later reactor disaster. No real weapons operating guide.
chapters.primary_evidence: Fallout New Vegas: Nellis, Pearl, Pete, Loyal, Volare!
chapters.length: 950-1100 substantive words; use the factual developments assigned here, never padding.

chapters.title: The vault under the Strip
chapters.job: Explore Vault 21's use of gambling to settle disputes and its later transformation under House. Develop Sarah Weintraub's hotel and the sealed sections as a case of adaptation instead of simple total collapse.
chapters.facts: Vault 21 resolves disputes through gambling. Mr. House wins control through a wager accepted by its residents. Much of the vault is filled with concrete, while an accessible section becomes a hotel managed by Sarah Weintraub. Some former residents establish lives elsewhere on the Strip.
chapters.boundary: Do not invent a secret army in the sealed sections or claim the wager had informed consent from every person. No exact concrete quantity.
chapters.primary_evidence: Fallout New Vegas: Vault 21, Sarah Weintraub and Michael Angelo dialogue.
chapters.length: 950-1100 substantive words; use the factual developments assigned here, never padding.

chapters.title: The overseer who would not comply
chapters.job: Introduce Vault 81 through its living public community and original overseer's sabotage of the secret medical experiment. Follow the missed scientist notifications, sealed research section and growing disconnection.
chapters.facts: Overseer Dr. Olivette opposes the planned use of residents as disease subjects. Only a small research team reaches the hidden section; she prevents the intended experiment on the population. The public vault develops into a functioning community while the separated researchers continue work with limited resources.
chapters.boundary: Her correct name is Olivette, not Olivia, and she is distinct from current overseer Gwen McNamara. Vault 81 was not designed as a control vault.
chapters.primary_evidence: Fallout 4: Vault 81 original overseer's terminal, research communication terminal.
chapters.length: 950-1100 substantive words; use the factual developments assigned here, never padding.

chapters.title: Curie and the last dose
chapters.job: Continue Vault 81 through the child Austin, the mole-rat outbreak, the sealed lab, Curie and the cure choice. Develop Curie's work after her human colleagues and the everyday community outside.
chapters.facts: Austin falls ill after a mole-rat bite. The Sole Survivor explores the hidden lab and finds Curie, who has developed a cure. A single available dose creates a choice if the protagonist was infected. Curie can leave the vault and later pursue a new form and research with the player.
chapters.boundary: Do not imply the treatment immediately cures every disease or that Curie herself initiated Olivette's sabotage. No claim the protagonist always becomes infected.
chapters.primary_evidence: Fallout 4: Hole in the Wall, Curie dialogue, research laboratory records.
chapters.length: 950-1100 substantive words; use the factual developments assigned here, never padding.

chapters.title: Five years of recovery
chapters.job: Develop Vault 95 through successful rehabilitation, residents' routines and the hidden cache released by an infiltrating employee. Follow Cait's later visit as a separate use of a surviving medical resource.
chapters.facts: Vault 95 gathers people recovering from addiction and supports a period of sobriety. A concealed Vault-Tec agent opens a hidden supply of addictive substances after five years, provoking the planned crisis. Long afterward, Cait can seek treatment with the Sole Survivor at its surviving detox facility.
chapters.boundary: Do not say the treatment guarantees an uncomplicated lifelong recovery. No drug recipes, modern medical advice or invented relapse rates.
chapters.primary_evidence: Fallout 4: Vault 95 resident records and Vault-Tec agent log, Benign Intervention.
chapters.length: 950-1100 substantive words; use the factual developments assigned here, never padding.

chapters.title: The experiments that never began as planned
chapters.job: Compare two unfinished or altered projects, Vault 114 and Vault 118, with separate concrete stories. Explain the wealthy residents promised facilities unlike the plan, Soup Can Harry's interview, and the later hotel robobrains and murder inquiry.
chapters.facts: Vault 114 is reached through Park Street Station; Nick Valentine is held there by Skinny Malone's gang. Its intended experiment places wealthy residents under poor conditions and an unsuitable overseer chosen through interviews including Soup Can Harry. Vault 118 beneath the Cliff's Edge Hotel was intended to divide rich and poor, but only the wealthy section was completed and its residents became robobrains. Brain Dead investigates a later murder there.
chapters.boundary: Do not describe either original social experiment as completed exactly as planned. Do not conflate Nick with a Vault-Tec creation, or reveal an invented Vault 118 ending.
chapters.primary_evidence: Fallout 4: Unlikely Valentine, Vault 114 interviews; Far Harbor: Brain Dead, Vault 118 terminals. Brain Dead, Ezra Parker reveal dialogue and player report to Maxwell; access-qualified sources recorded in benchmark source checks.
chapters.length: 950-1100 substantive words; use the factual developments assigned here, never padding.

chapters.title: The unfinished vault and the willing overseer
chapters.job: Develop Vault 88 as the player's opportunity to operate, soften or reject experiments after the war. Follow Barstow, Clem and configurable devices through the Workshop story. Explain that technical survival leaves a decision with the new overseer.
chapters.facts: Overseer Barstow survives as a ghoul in unfinished Vault 88. The Sole Survivor can build a settlement and assist her experiments with Clem and other volunteers. The experiments have different selectable parameters, including less harmful options. The player can oppose Barstow or continue along her preferred direction.
chapters.boundary: No one ending is compulsory. Do not list the most harmful device settings as a how-to or claim a voluntary building task gives residents full knowledge of every hidden parameter.
chapters.primary_evidence: Fallout 4 Vault-Tec Workshop: Vault 88, Barstow, Clem and experiment configuration choices.
chapters.length: 950-1100 substantive words; use the factual developments assigned here, never padding.

chapters.title: Reclamation after the promise
chapters.job: Finish at Vault 76 and its overseer's recordings. Explain a vault that functions as a shelter, Reclamation Day, the hidden order to secure silos and the survivors' responsibility to people outside. Briefly distinguish questions left open by the games from a total conspiracy answer, then end on rebuilding in Appalachia.
chapters.facts: Vault 76 is a control vault with a population chosen to rebuild. Its residents leave on Reclamation Day. The overseer is separately ordered to secure nuclear silos Alpha, Bravo and Charlie for Vault-Tec, disregarding competing claims. Her recordings follow her discovery of devastated Appalachia and growing doubts about the organization's judgment.
chapters.boundary: Use the original Fallout 76 vault and overseer story, not current live-service developments. Do not assert Vault-Tec launched the first bombs, a confirmed space-colony master plan, or that every vault was intended to kill everyone. No recap catalogue or CTA.
chapters.primary_evidence: Fallout 76: Vault 76 terminal entries, overseer's mission and original journey holotapes.
chapters.length: 950-1100 substantive words; use the factual developments assigned here, never padding.

episodes.title: The Disappearance of the Dwemer Explained to Fall Asleep To | Elder Scrolls Lore
episodes.angle: An archaeological history: surviving cities and devices, the people and books around Kagrenac, contradictory accounts of Red Mountain, and theories held to what the games actually show.
episodes.scope: TES III Morrowind, TES II Daggerfall and TES V Skyrim with Dawnguard and Dragonborn, including their in-game books and dialogue. Full spoilers. No mods, Creation Club, developer forum fiction or ESO-specific new revelations.
episodes.planned_runtime: At least 150 minutes at 170 words per minute; estimate only.
forbidden: Original English narration only; no copied dialogue or competitor wording.
No invented journals, props, motives, dates, numerical probabilities or developer intent.
No mods, fan fiction, cut quests presented as playable canon, or unofficial endings.
No graphic violence or described self-harm methods; discuss consequences gently.
Only one optional subscribe plus listening location/day-or-night CTA in chapter one.
No trailers, repeated bedtime instructions, philosophical filler, repeated disclaimers or recaps.
All assigned chapters belong to one continuous narration. Resolve their local questions.

Do not state all Dwemer vanished without exception; Yagrum survives. No confirmed solution or definite last day reconstruction. Gods are present in the setting; describe Dwemer opposition to worship and attempts to understand divine power, not simplistic disbelief that any gods exist.

proof.primary: Morrowind and Skyrim ruins; Morrowind disappearance dialogue and Red Mountain accounts.
proof.facts: The Dwemer are an Elven people, often called Dwarves by outsiders. Their abandoned cities and surviving automata appear in Morrowind and Skyrim. Their disappearance is connected by several accounts to the Battle of Red Mountain and Kagrenac's work. Its exact mechanism and destination remain unresolved. Early orientation identifies Anumidium, the Heart, Sunder, Keening and Wraithguard; the Nerevarine's later intervention undoes enchantments and does not restore the Dwemer. These facts are developed in the existing Heart and tools chapters.
proof.boundary: No definitive solution, no fantasy claim that the Dwemer were tiny, no invented last night in a household.

proof.primary: Morrowind: Arkngthand and Nchuleftingth; Skyrim: Markarth; Dwemer histories in the games.
proof.facts: Dwemer sites exist in Morrowind, Skyrim and Hammerfell. Vvardenfell includes ruins such as Arkngthand and Nchuleftingth; Skyrim contains Markarth's inherited structures and numerous buried cities. Rourken's western migration is remembered in Hammerfell's lore. The Dwemer had different clans and city-states.
proof.boundary: No invented population census, continent-wide unified government or assertion a shared doorway means identical politics.

proof.primary: Skyrim: Understone Keep, Calcelmo dialogue, Nchuand-Zel.
proof.facts: Markarth uses Dwemer stone and metal buildings. Understone Keep contains Calcelmo's research, museum and excavation. A route leads into Nchuand-Zel, where automata and Falmer occupy spaces beneath the living city. Calcelmo studies material most residents use without deciphering.
proof.boundary: Do not re-narrate the Forsworn conspiracy or claim all Markarth walls preserve original Dwemer functions.

proof.primary: Morrowind and Skyrim: Dwemer automata, recoverable components and ruin layouts.
proof.facts: Dwemer spiders, spheres and centurions remain active in abandoned ruins. They have distinct forms and weapons, and often guard passages and machinery. They can contain soul gems and Dwemer metal components. Their survival is visible, but no complete technical blueprint is supplied to the player.
proof.boundary: Do not say every machine has a Dwemer soul or that steam alone explains its power. No invented maintenance robots servicing every ruin.

proof.primary: Skyrim: Elder Knowledge; Dragonborn: The Path of Knowledge and Kagrumez.
proof.facts: Septimus provides an attunement sphere and blank lexicon for the Skyrim Elder Scroll journey. A Dwemer mechanism accepts the sphere to permit entry into Blackreach. Nchardak uses control cubes for its systems; Kagrumez uses resonance gems. The tools are specific to their mechanisms.
proof.boundary: No universal password, modern computer-network analogy stretched into fact or assertion every ruin responds to the same frequency.

proof.primary: Morrowind: Divine Metaphysics dialogue; Skyrim Dawnguard: Arkngthamz tonal lock.
proof.facts: Kagrenac is a chief tonal architect. Morrowind's Divine Metaphysics discussion connects his tools, sacred tones and Anumidium. Skyrim includes resonator mechanisms and a tonal lock at Arkngthamz. Sound and crafted resonance are part of Dwemer work.
proof.boundary: No real-world frequency values, theory of everything, certainty every Dwemer wall rewrites reality, or claim modern acoustic physics proves the lore.

proof.primary: Skyrim: Hard Answers, Calcelmo's Stone; Dawnguard: Gelebor dialogue, The Falmer: A Study.
proof.facts: Snow Elves seek refuge with the Dwemer after defeat by the Nords. The Dwemer impose harmful terms associated with the loss of sight and enslavement. Calcelmo's Stone preserves a bilingual proclamation concerning this relationship. Gelebor describes the later Falmer and questions aspects of their degeneration. In Hard Answers, Gallus's journal is written in Falmer. Enthir uses Calcelmo's bilingual inscription to translate it.
proof.boundary: Do not claim fungus alone scientifically explains every change or that every Snow Elf entered Dwemer custody. No exact universal timetable.

proof.primary: Skyrim: The Falmer: A Study, Gelebor dialogue and ruins.
proof.facts: Accounts of the Falmer describe rebellion against Dwemer masters and prolonged underground conflict. When the Dwemer disappear, Falmer remain and inhabit parts of their former cities. Skyrim ruins show Falmer, chaurus and automata in overlapping territories.
proof.boundary: No complete battle chronology or claim the Falmer defeated all Dwemer in a final battle. Do not make Falmer transformed Dwemer.

proof.primary: Morrowind: The War of the First Council, The Battle of Red Mountain, Nerevar at Red Mountain.
proof.facts: Chimer leader Indoril Nerevar and Dwemer king Dumac are associated with the First Council and the overthrow of Nordic dominance in Resdayn. The groups coexist despite major cultural and religious differences. The alliance later breaks down around Red Mountain and the Heart.
proof.boundary: Do not invent private speeches, a written treaty clause, or unanimity among either people. Avoid unsupported exact dates.

proof.primary: In-game Rourken histories, Volendrung artifact traditions and Volenfell lore.
proof.facts: The Rourken reject the alliance with the Chimer and migrate west. A tradition says their leader throws Volendrung and follows it to the future homeland. Dwemer sites remain in Hammerfell. Their geographical separation complicates an explanation confined to the destruction of one fortress.
proof.boundary: The thrown-hammer account is a legend, not a measured trajectory. No claim geographical reach proves a specific soul-network mechanism.

proof.primary: Skyrim Dawnguard: The Aetherium Wars, Katria's journal, Lost to the Ages.
proof.facts: The Aetherium Wars describes aetherium research and cooperation among Skyrim Dwemer cities, followed by fighting over access to the forge and material. The book is attributed to Taron Dreth. Lost to the Ages reveals Katria's work and the surviving Aetherium Forge. Bthalft is the shared forge destination, not the fourth member of the alliance. In Morrowind Vivec and Yagrum can be involved in obtaining or activating protection depending on the route. The Nerevarine uses the tools against the Heart's enchantments.
chapters.boundary: Do not narrate gameplay damage numbers or equate Skyrim's changed Keening mechanics with a canon solved experiment. Wraithguard is not a weapon or the Heart itself.
chapters.primary_evidence: Morrowind: Kagrenac's Tools, Vivec's plan, Yagrum dialogue, Keening and Sunder retrieval.
chapters.length: 950-1100 substantive words; use the factual developments assigned here, never padding.

chapters.title: Kagrenac and the brass god
chapters.job: Explain the Anumidium project as an attempt to construct a god using the Heart. Develop Kagrenac's ambition through documents and his colleagues' reservations rather than imagined villain dialogue. Introduce Dumac's uncertain knowledge without resolving it.
chapters.facts: Kagrenac develops Anumidium, also called Numidium, in connection with the Heart of Lorkhan. He creates the tools and works with tonal methods. Surviving accounts disagree over who knew what and how the project was revealed. Yagrum reports that colleagues disputed Kagrenac's conclusions.
chapters.boundary: No claim every Dwemer voted for ascension or agreed to become a skin. Do not claim Dumac's exact private knowledge is settled.
chapters.primary_evidence: Morrowind: Divine Metaphysics discussion, Yagrum dialogue, The Battle of Red Mountain, Nerevar at Red Mountain.
chapters.length: 950-1100 substantive words; use the factual developments assigned here, never padding.

chapters.title: The war inside the alliance
chapters.job: Return to Nerevar, Dumac and Dagoth at the moment the coalition breaks. Compare the discovery of the Heart project and the different loyalties, then take the conflict to Red Mountain without resolving the competing final accounts prematurely.
chapters.facts: Accounts link the First Council's collapse to discovery of Kagrenac's work. Nerevar opposes the threat he sees in it. Dagoth reports or is involved in the discovery in surviving accounts. Chimer and Dwemer go to war. Their leaders and the Heart chamber become central to later narratives. Nerevar at Red Mountain explicitly says Kagrenac's new god was hidden from Dumac. Vivec's The Battle of Red Mountain describes Dumac's anger at interference without the same explicit assurance of ignorance. This is a concrete difference in the pre-battle accounts, not a settled fact about Dumac's mind.
chapters.boundary: No newly invented battle speech, exact army strength, reconciled timeline or assumption a partisan book is an omniscient camera.
chapters.primary_evidence: Morrowind: The War of the First Council, The Battle of Red Mountain, Nerevar at Red Mountain, Progress of Truth.
chapters.length: 950-1100 substantive words; use the factual developments assigned here, never padding.

chapters.title: The stories of the Red Moment
chapters.job: Compare Vivec's Battle of Red Mountain with the Ashlander account Nerevar at Red Mountain and the Nordic tradition in Five Songs of King Wulfharth. Explain their concrete disagreements over alliances, deaths and the use of the tools. Let each account be understandable before comparing.
chapters.facts: Vivec's account ties the disappearance to Kagrenac using the tools under pressure. Nerevar at Red Mountain describes Dagoth killing Kagrenac and an Azura-guided use of the tools that strips the Dwemer's borrowed immortality. Nordic accounts assign different alignments and roles. They cannot all be read as one straightforward eyewitness sequence.
chapters.boundary: No final canonical reconstruction or automatic claim every discrepancy is a Dragon Break. Do not turn the chapter into an abstract lecture about unreliable narrators.
chapters.primary_evidence: Morrowind: The Battle of Red Mountain; Nerevar at Red Mountain; Five Songs of King Wulfharth.
chapters.length: 950-1100 substantive words; use the factual developments assigned here, never padding.

chapters.title: The gods who inherited the tools
chapters.job: Follow the Tribunal and Dagoth Ur after the disappearance, their relationship to the Heart and the Nerevarine's intervention. Explain what the later experiment proves about access to divine power and what it leaves unanswered about the earlier people.
chapters.facts: Vivec, Almalexia and Sotha Sil draw divine power from the Heart. Dagoth Ur also draws on it and pursues Akulakhan, another giant construction. The Nerevarine uses Kagrenac's tools to break the Heart's enchantments, ending Dagoth Ur's dependence and cutting off the Tribunal's source.
chapters.boundary: The Heart is freed from the enchantments rather than necessarily annihilated. Do not claim every user disappears like the Dwemer or the Nerevarine becomes a Dwemer.
chapters.primary_evidence: Morrowind main quest: Vivec's plan, Dagoth Ur dialogue, Akulakhan chamber and ending.
chapters.length: 950-1100 substantive words; use the factual developments assigned here, never padding.

chapters.title: The brass giant after its makers
chapters.job: Develop Numidium's later place in Tiber Septim's conquest, the Mantella and the events around Daggerfall. Distinguish the later activations and documented Warp in the West from speculation about Red Mountain.
chapters.facts: Numidium later appears in accounts of Tiber Septim's conquests, associated with a different power source, the Mantella. Daggerfall's main quest revolves around the Totem and Mantella and leads to competing outcomes later reflected in the Warp in the West. Those later events involve temporal contradiction.
chapters.boundary: Do not treat The Arcturian Heresy as uncontested biography or a later Dragon Break as proof of the earlier disappearance's mechanism. Do not invent a single mandatory Daggerfall winner.
chapters.primary_evidence: Daggerfall main quest and endings; The Warp in the West; The Arcturian Heresy as a partisan account.
chapters.length: 950-1100 substantive words; use the factual developments assigned here, never padding.

chapters.title: Arniel's smaller experiment
chapters.job: Follow Arniel Gane's errands, warped soul gem, Dwemer convectors and Keening experiment at the College. Explain his disappearance and the shade summoning result as a local event, then compare its differences from Kagrenac's setup.
chapters.facts: Arniel investigates the Dwemer disappearance. He asks for Dwemer cogs, a warped soul gem heated at convectors and Keening. In the final experiment he strikes the gem and vanishes. The player gains the ability to summon Arniel's Shade. He did not use the Heart of Lorkhan or the full original set of tools.
chapters.boundary: No claim this proves all Dwemer became summonable ghosts, that the player absorbed them, or that the shade explains an entire people's destination.
chapters.primary_evidence: Skyrim: Arniel's Endeavor, Arniel dialogue and final experiment.
chapters.length: 950-1100 substantive words; use the factual developments assigned here, never padding.

chapters.title: What the empty cities still keep
chapters.job: Finish by weighing three bounded readings against specific already established constraints: a catastrophic failure, a transformation tied to Numidium, or displacement beyond ordinary existence. Bring Yagrum's absence, divergent Red Mountain accounts, distant clans and Arniel's imperfect analogy into the comparison. Close at an ordinary surviving door or machine, not a new teaser or recap list.
chapters.facts: The disappearance's timing, Kagrenac's Heart project, Yagrum's survival during absence and functioning ruins are important constraints. A catastrophic failure and Numidium-related transformation are interpretations, not shown outcomes. The widely circulated skin-of-Numidium interpretation is not a confirmed game revelation. No surviving quest supplies a final destination or complete means of reversing it.
chapters.boundary: No certainty about zero-summing, universal soul absorption, a secretly living civilization or future game revelations. Prefer a small number of reasoned possibilities to an exhaustive speculative list. No CTA or sequel promise.
chapters.primary_evidence: Comparison of the game evidence assigned above; clearly identified interpretations, not additional facts.
